findings.title: queued timestamp is evaluated once at import time
findings.body: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` calls timezone.now() when the dataclass class is defined, not when an AssignmentSource is constructed. Every instance created without an explicit queued value therefore shares the process/import-time timestamp instead of its creation time. If queued is later used for ordering, staleness, or debounce decisions, those decisions will be wrong; it should use field(default_factory=timezone.now).

findings.title: AssignmentSource dict passed to Celery contains a non-JSON-serializable datetime
findings.body: assignment_source.to_dict() uses dataclasses.asdict(), so the queued value remains a datetime object. That dict is placed directly in sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async(kwargs=...), whose arguments must be serializable by the task serializer. On the inbound-assignment path this will fail to enqueue the outbound task (e.g. with a serialization/EncodeError) instead of performing the filtered sync, whereas the eager self.tasks() tests do not exercise real serialization. queued should be serialized to an ISO string (and parsed back in from_dict) or removed from the wire dict.

findings.title: New assignment_source kwarg is unconditionally passed to all sync_assignee_outbound implementations
findings.body: The task now calls installation.sync_assignee_outbound(..., assignment_source=parsed_assignment_source) for every installation. The abstract method allows **kwargs, but concrete issue-sync implementations are not required to accept an assignment_source keyword (several define only external_issue, user and assign). For such implementations this unconditional new kwarg raises TypeError and breaks all outbound assignee syncs, not just ones originating from an inbound webhook. Either only pass it when supported, keep passing it via **kwargs-compatible signatures after updating all implementations, or drop it since the value is only needed for the should_sync check already performed here.
